at vaccinere.explanation: "At vaccinere" means "to vaccinate": a doctor or nurse gives you protection so your body can fight a disease. Mod (against) marks the disease: vaccinere mod influenza (vaccinate against the flu). To say you get vaccinated, use at lade sig vaccinere (to let yourself be vaccinated).

sentence.da: Lægen vil **vaccinere** alle børn i klassen mod mæslinger.
sentence.en: The doctor will vaccinate all the children in the class against measles.

at vade.explanation: "At vade" means "to wade", to walk through water or mud that reaches your legs. It is also used for walking through deep snow.

sentence.da: Vi kan **vade** over åen, fordi vandet ikke er dybt.
sentence.en: We can wade across the stream because the water is not deep.

at vakle.explanation: "At vakle" means "to wobble" and "to waver". A tired person vakler when walking unsteadily. About a decision or a belief, it means being unsure and close to changing your mind.

sentence.da: Stolen vil **vakle**, fordi det ene ben er kortere.
sentence.en: The chair will wobble because one leg is shorter.

at vande.explanation: "At vande" means "to water" plants, flowers and lawns: Hun vander plænen om aftenen (She waters the lawn in the evening). It comes from vand (water).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **vande** blomsterne, fordi det ikke har regnet.
sentence.en: I have to water the flowers because it has not rained.

at vandre.explanation: "At vandre" means "to hike" and "to wander": to go on foot for a long time, often in nature, for the pleasure of it: Vi vandrer langs kysten hvert efterår (We hike along the coast every fall). It can also mean to walk without hurry or goal: Han vandrede rundt i byen (He wandered around town).

sentence.da: Vi vil **vandre** fem timer i bjergene og sove i telt.
sentence.en: We want to hike five hours in the mountains and sleep in a tent.

at vare.explanation: "At vare" means "to last", telling how long something goes on. It is mostly used about events and time, with the length after it: Filmen varer to timer (The movie lasts two hours).

sentence.da: Mødet vil **vare** i cirka en time.
sentence.en: The meeting will last about an hour.

at variere.explanation: "At variere" means "to vary". It works two ways: something is not always the same by itself, as in Prisen varierer (The price varies), or you do it on purpose, as in Jeg varierer menuen (I vary the menu).

sentence.da: Temperaturen kan **variere** meget fra dag til dag.
sentence.en: The temperature can vary a lot from day to day.

at vaske.explanation: "At vaske" means "to wash", for clothes, dishes, your hands or the car: Jeg vasker bilen (I wash the car). To wash yourself, say vaske sig (to wash oneself). At vaske op means "to do the dishes".

sentence.da: Jeg vil **vaske** tøjet i dag.
sentence.en: I want to wash the clothes today.

at vaske gulv.explanation: "At vaske gulv" means "to mop the floor" and is said without gulvet (the floor): Vi vasker gulv om lørdagen (We mop the floor on Saturdays). For one spill, use at tørre op (to wipe up).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **vaske gulv**, fordi det er meget beskidt.
sentence.en: I have to mop the floor because it is very dirty.

at vaske op.explanation: "At vaske op" means "to do the dishes" by hand: Hvem vasker op i dag? (Who is doing the dishes today?). Do not mix it up with at vaske (to wash), which is used for clothes, hands or the car.

sentence.da: Jeg skal **vaske op** efter maden.
sentence.en: I have to do the dishes after the meal.

at vaske sig.explanation: "At vaske sig" means "to wash yourself". The little word sig (oneself) becomes mig (myself) when you talk about yourself: jeg vasker mig (I wash myself). If you wash something else, you drop it: at vaske hænder (to wash hands) or at vaske tøj (to wash clothes).

sentence.da: Han skal **vaske sig** før maden.
sentence.en: He has to wash himself before the meal.

at vaske tøj.explanation: "At vaske tøj" means "to do laundry", literally to wash clothes: Min søster vasker tøj hver søndag (My sister does laundry every Sunday). For dishes, say at vaske op (to wash the dishes).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **vaske tøj**, fordi jeg ikke har flere rene sokker.
sentence.en: I have to do laundry because I have no more clean socks.

at vedkende sig.explanation: "At vedkende sig" means "to acknowledge", to say openly that something is yours or is true, such as a mistake or a responsibility. It is mostly used for uncomfortable things that you take ownership of.

sentence.da: Han har svært ved at **vedkende sig** sine fejl.
sentence.en: He finds it hard to acknowledge his faults.

at vedligeholde.explanation: "At vedligeholde" means "to maintain": to keep something in good condition with regular care, like a house, a garden, a road, or a machine. It is not used for claiming something. For that meaning of maintain, Danes say at hævde (to claim).

sentence.da: Man skal **vedligeholde** træværket hvert år, fordi regn skader det.
sentence.en: You must maintain the woodwork every year because rain damages it.

at vedlægge.explanation: "At vedlægge" means "to enclose", to put a document in with a letter, an email or an application. It is a written word; in speech people more often say at sende med (to send along).

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne **vedlægge** mit CV til ansøgningen.
sentence.en: I would like to enclose my résumé with the application.

at vedrøre.explanation: "At vedrøre" means "to concern", to be about or to affect someone or something. The thing it is about comes straight after: Sagen vedrører dig (The matter concerns you). Letters and emails often start with Vedrørende (Regarding), a form of this word.

sentence.da: Reglen kan **vedrøre** alle elever i skolen.
sentence.en: The rule can concern all students in the school.

at vedtage.explanation: "At vedtage" means "to pass (a law)" or "to adopt", when a group officially agrees on something. It is used for parliaments, councils and boards: Folketinget vedtog loven (Parliament passed the law).

sentence.da: Byrådet vil **vedtage** det nye budget i næste uge.
sentence.en: The city council will pass the new budget next week.

at veje.explanation: "At veje" means "to weigh". It works two ways: you weigh something on a scale, or you have a certain weight. Jeg vejer 70 kilo (I weigh 70 kilos). The thing you weigh comes right after: Jeg vejer pakken (I weigh the package).

sentence.da: Man kan **veje** maden på en vægt.
sentence.en: You can weigh the food on a scale.

at vejlede.explanation: "At vejlede" means "to guide" or "to advise", to help someone find the right way with explanations and tips, often as part of a job at a school or an employment office. It is built from vej (way) and lede (lead).

sentence.da: Læreren vil **vejlede** eleverne, når de skriver opgaven.
sentence.en: The teacher will guide the students when they write the assignment.

at veksle.explanation: "At veksle" means "to exchange (money)", changing it from one currency to another. It also means to break a big bill into smaller ones: Kan du veksle en hundredkroneseddel? (Can you break a hundred-krone bill?)

sentence.da: Hvor kan jeg **veksle** euro til danske kroner?
sentence.en: Where can I exchange euros for Danish kroner?

at velsigne.explanation: "At velsigne" means "to bless", to ask for good things for someone or to declare something holy, as is done in a church. It is built from vel (well) and signe (bless).

sentence.da: Præsten vil **velsigne** parret ved brylluppet.
sentence.en: The priest will bless the couple at the wedding.

at vende.explanation: "At vende" means "to turn" something over or around: Jeg vender kortet (I turn the card over). For turning in a direction, say at dreje (to turn): Drej til venstre (Turn left).

sentence.da: Du kan **vende** bladet og læse videre.
sentence.en: You can turn the page and read on.

at vende sig.explanation: "At vende sig" means "to turn around" with your own body: Han vendte sig og smilede (He turned around and smiled). Do not mix it up with at vænne sig til (to get used to).

sentence.da: Han vil **vende sig** og se på mig.
sentence.en: He wants to turn around and look at me.

at vende tilbage.explanation: "At vende tilbage" means "to return", to come back to a place or a topic: Han vender tilbage til byen (He returns to the city). It is also a polite way to say you will answer later: Jeg vender tilbage til dig (I will get back to you).

sentence.da: Vi vil **vende tilbage** til Danmark næste år.
sentence.en: We want to return to Denmark next year.

at vente.explanation: "At vente" means "to wait": Jeg venter på bussen (I am waiting for the bus). It can also mean "to expect": Hun venter barn (She is expecting a baby).

sentence.da: Børn kan ikke **vente** til jul.
sentence.en: Kids cannot wait for Christmas.

at vente på.explanation: "At vente på" means "to wait for" someone or something: Jeg venter på dig (I am waiting for you). The little word på (on) always stays with it.

sentence.da: Jeg skal **vente på** bussen.
sentence.en: I have to wait for the bus.

at verificere.explanation: "At verificere" means "to verify", to make sure that something is true or correct, for example who a person is. Banks and websites use it for identity: at verificere sin identitet (to verify your identity).

sentence.da: Journalisten vil **verificere** kilderne, fordi nyheden kan være falsk.
sentence.en: The journalist wants to verify the sources because the news may be false.

at vide.explanation: "At vide" means "to know" a fact: Jeg ved det ikke (I do not know). For knowing a person or a place, Danish uses a different word, at kende (to know someone).

sentence.da: Du skal **vide** dit telefonnummer.
sentence.en: You need to know your phone number.

at videreføre.explanation: "At videreføre" means "to continue", in the sense of carrying on something that already exists, such as a tradition or a project that others began. For plain "keep going", say at fortsætte (to continue): Jeg fortsætter med at læse (I keep on reading).

sentence.da: Hun vil **videreføre** familiens firma, når hendes far går på pension.
sentence.en: She wants to carry on the family business when her father retires.

at videregive.explanation: "At videregive" means "to pass on", to give information or an object on to another person. It is the careful word for private information, where passing it on needs permission.

sentence.da: Lægen må ikke **videregive** dine oplysninger til andre.
sentence.en: The doctor may not pass on your information to others.

at vidne.explanation: "At vidne" means "to testify", to tell a court what you saw or know. The same word also names the person: et vidne (a witness). With om (about) it means to show: Resultatet vidner om hårdt arbejde (The result shows hard work).

sentence.da: Hun skal **vidne** i retten, fordi hun så ulykken.
sentence.en: She must testify in court because she saw the accident.

at vifte.explanation: "At vifte" means "to wave (something)" back and forth, usually with med (with): Han vifter med en avis (He waves a newspaper). To wave to a person, use at vinke (to wave to someone) instead. En vifte is also a fan.

sentence.da: Børnene skal **vifte** med små flag, når kongen kommer.
sentence.en: The children will wave small flags when the king comes.

at ville.explanation: "At ville" means "to want to": Jeg vil have en kop kaffe (I want a cup of coffee). Adding gerne (gladly) makes it polite: Jeg vil gerne have en kop kaffe (I would like a cup of coffee). Vil is about wanting, not just will: for a duty, use skal (have to): Jeg skal gå (I have to go).

sentence.da: Børn kan altid **ville** have mere.
sentence.en: Kids can always want more.

at vinde.explanation: "At vinde" means "to win": Hun vinder løbet (She wins the race).

sentence.da: Holdet med flest mål vil **vinde** kampen.
sentence.en: The team with the most goals will win the match.

at vinke.explanation: "At vinke" means "to wave" your hand: Hun vinker til mig (She waves at me). Use til (to) for who you wave at, and add farvel (goodbye) to wave goodbye: Han vinkede farvel (He waved goodbye).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **vinke** til dig, når toget kører.
sentence.en: I will wave to you when the train leaves.

at vippe.explanation: "At vippe" means "to tip" or "to rock", to move up on one side and down on the other. En vippe is a seesaw, and Vip ikke med stolen! (Do not rock the chair!) is said to children who lean back.

sentence.da: Hvis bordet står skævt, kan det **vippe**.
sentence.en: If the table stands crooked, it can rock.

at virke.explanation: "At virke" means "to work", for things that function, and also "to seem": Bilen virker ikke (The car does not work). Han virker træt (He seems tired).

sentence.da: Telefonen vil ikke **virke** i dag.
sentence.en: The phone won't work today.

at vise.explanation: "At vise" means "to show": Jeg viser billedet (I show the picture). When you show someone something, the person comes first, with no word for "to" in front: Hun viser mig bogen (She shows me the book). Vis mig means "Show me".

sentence.da: Kan du **vise** mig vej?
sentence.en: Can you show me the way?

at vise sig.explanation: "At vise sig" means "to turn out", when you find out how something really is: Det viste sig, at bilen var gratis (It turned out that the car was free). Hun viste sig at være meget flink (She turned out to be very nice).

sentence.da: Det kan **vise sig**, at han har ret.
sentence.en: It may turn out that he is right.

at visne.explanation: "At visne" means "to wither", when a plant dries up and goes limp because it lacks water or is dying. Danes also use it for something fading away, such as a smile: Smilet visnede (The smile faded).

sentence.da: Blomsterne vil **visne**, når du glemmer at vande dem.
sentence.en: The flowers will wither when you forget to water them.

at visualisere.explanation: "At visualisere" means "to visualize", to picture something in your mind or to show information as a drawing or graph: Jeg kan godt visualisere huset (I can picture the house).

sentence.da: Vi bruger et diagram til at **visualisere** tallene.
sentence.en: We use a chart to visualize the figures.

at vokse.explanation: "At vokse" means "to grow", for children, plants and things: Børn vokser hurtigt (Children grow fast). To grow up is at vokse op: Jeg voksede op i Odense (I grew up in Odense). To grow tomatoes, use at dyrke (to cultivate).

sentence.da: Planterne kan **vokse** meget hurtigt.
sentence.en: The plants can grow very fast.

at vokse op.explanation: "At vokse op" means "to grow up", to spend your childhood somewhere: Jeg voksede op i Jylland (I grew up in Jutland). Without op, at vokse means "to grow", for example plants: Træet vokser hurtigt (The tree grows quickly).

sentence.da: Mine børn skal **vokse op** på landet.
sentence.en: My children will grow up in the countryside.

at vove.explanation: "At vove" means "to dare", to do something even though it might go wrong. In everyday speech Danes mostly say at turde (to dare): Jeg tør ikke (I do not dare).

sentence.da: Ingen vil **vove** at gå ind i det mørke hus.
sentence.en: No one dares to go into the dark house.

at vride.explanation: "At vride" means "to twist" or "to wring", to turn something hard with your hands, often to squeeze the water out. With sig (oneself) it means to writhe: Han vred sig af smerte (He writhed in pain).

sentence.da: Du skal **vride** vandet ud af håndklædet.
sentence.en: You must wring the water out of the towel.

at vrimle.explanation: "At vrimle" means "to swarm" or "to teem", when a place is full of many small things moving about, such as people or insects. It is followed by med (with): Gaden vrimler med mennesker (The street teems with people).

sentence.da: Om sommeren kan stranden **vrimle** med børn og turister.
sentence.en: In the summer, the beach can swarm with children and tourists.

at vurdere.explanation: "At vurdere" means "to evaluate", to form an opinion about how good, big or valuable something is. It is also used for setting a price: Huset bliver vurderet til tre millioner (The house is valued at three million).

sentence.da: Lægen skal **vurdere**, om skaden er alvorlig.
sentence.en: The doctor must assess whether the injury is serious.

at vågne.explanation: "At vågne" means "to wake up" by yourself: Jeg vågner klokken syv (I wake up at seven). When someone else wakes you, Danish uses at vække (to wake someone).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **vågne** klokken syv.
sentence.en: I have to wake up at seven.

at vågne op.explanation: "At vågne op" means "to wake up", the moment you become awake. People often just say at vågne (to wake up), so the op (up) is optional. Do not mix it up with at stå op (to get out of bed).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **vågne op** tidligt i morgen.
sentence.en: I want to wake up early tomorrow.

at vædde.explanation: "At vædde" means "to bet". What you bet on follows på (on): Vi vædder på vejret (We bet on the weather).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **vædde** på, at holdet vinder i aften.
sentence.en: I will bet that the team wins tonight.

at vække.explanation: "At vække" means "to wake someone": Jeg vækker børnene klokken syv (I wake the kids at seven). To wake up yourself, say at vågne (to wake up): Jeg vågnede tidligt (I woke up early).

sentence.da: Kan du **vække** mig klokken seks?
sentence.en: Can you wake me at six?

at vælge.explanation: "At vælge" means "to choose" or "to pick": Jeg vælger den røde (I choose the red one). Et valg means both "a choice" and "an election".

sentence.da: Du må **vælge** rød eller blå.
sentence.en: You may choose red or blue.

at vælte.explanation: "At vælte" means "to knock over" and "to tip over": Jeg vælter koppen (I knock over the cup). Something can also go over by itself: Træet væltede (The tree fell over).

forms.en: I have knocked over / tipped over

sentence.da: Pas på, du kan **vælte** glasset!
sentence.en: Be careful, you might knock over the glass!

at vænne sig af med.explanation: "At vænne sig af med" means "to get out of the habit of", to stop doing something you used to do regularly. It is the opposite of at vænne sig til (to get used to), so af means away from and til means toward. The thing you leave behind comes after med.

forms.en: to get out of the habit of
I get out of the habit of
I got out of the habit of

forms.da: jeg har vænnet mig af med
forms.en: I have gotten out of the habit of

sentence.da: Han vil **vænne sig af med** at spise sukker hver dag.
sentence.en: He wants to get out of the habit of eating sugar every day.

at vænne sig til.explanation: "At vænne sig til" means "to get used to": Jeg vænner mig til kulden (I am getting used to the cold). Once it is done, say vant til: Jeg er vant til kulden (I am used to the cold).

sentence.da: Det tager tid at **vænne sig til** et nyt sted.
sentence.en: It takes time to get used to a new place.

at værdsætte.explanation: "At værdsætte" means "to appreciate", to value something and be glad of it: Jeg værdsætter din hjælp (I appreciate your help). It never means to go up in value, as in English; for that say at stige i værdi (to rise in value).

sentence.da: Man skal kunne **værdsætte** de små ting i livet.
sentence.en: You have to be able to appreciate the small things in life.

at være.explanation: "At være" means "to be": Jeg er glad (I am happy). The form er is the same for everyone: jeg er (I am), han er (he is), vi er (we are).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **være** hjemme i dag.
sentence.en: I want to be at home today.

at være bange for.explanation: "At være bange for" means "to be afraid of": Jeg er bange for edderkopper (I am afraid of spiders). Before a verb, add at: Jeg er bange for at falde (I am afraid of falling).

sentence.da: Børn kan **være bange for** mørket.
sentence.en: Children can be afraid of the dark.

at være enig.explanation: "At være enig" means "to agree" and literally says "to be agreed": Jeg er enig med dig (I agree with you). To agree on a thing, add i: Vi er enige i det (We agree on that).

sentence.da: Jeg kan **være enig** i det.
sentence.en: I can agree with that.

at være i tvivl.explanation: "At være i tvivl" means "to be in doubt", or to be unsure: Jeg er i tvivl om svaret (I am unsure about the answer). Use om (about) before the thing you are unsure of.

sentence.da: Når man ikke ved svaret, kan man **være i tvivl**.
sentence.en: When you do not know the answer, you can be in doubt.

at være kærester.explanation: "At være kærester" means "to be dating", or to be a couple: Vi har været kærester i to år (We have been a couple for two years). One person is en kæreste (a boyfriend or girlfriend).

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne **være kærester** med dig.
sentence.en: I would like us to be a couple.

at være med.explanation: "At være med" means "to take part", to join what others are doing: Er du med? (Are you in?). It also means "to follow along": Jeg er ikke helt med (I am not quite following).

forms.en: to take part / be in on it
I take part / am in on it
I took part / was in on it
I have taken part / been in on it

sentence.da: Vil du **være med**, når vi spiller fodbold?
sentence.en: Do you want to join in when we play soccer?

at være nødt til.explanation: "At være nødt til" means "to have to", when you have no other choice: Jeg er nødt til at gå nu (I have to go now). It is stronger than skal (must / am going to), which can be just a plan: Jeg skal på arbejde (I am going to work).

sentence.da: Når bussen er væk, kan vi **være nødt til** at gå.
sentence.en: When the bus is gone, we may have to walk.

at være oppe at køre.explanation: "At være oppe at køre" means "to be worked up", to be tense, excited and full of restless energy. It can be about stress or about excitement.

forms.da: Han var oppe at køre i går
Vær ikke så oppe at køre
forms.en: Do not be so worked up

sentence.da: Han plejer at **være oppe at køre**, når der er eksamen.
sentence.en: He tends to be worked up when there is an exam.

at være på bar bund.explanation: "At være på bar bund" means "to be at a total loss", to have no idea what to do or answer, with nothing to build on. Literally it is to be on bare bottom.

forms.en: I am at a total loss
She was at a total loss
We are at a total loss

sentence.da: Han kan **være på bar bund** til eksamen, fordi han ikke har læst.
sentence.en: He can be at a total loss at the exam because he has not studied.

at være på herrens mark.explanation: "At være på Herrens mark" means "to be completely lost", to be totally confused or wrong about something. It is about understanding, not about finding your way. Literally it is to be on the Lord's field.

forms.da: Jeg er helt på Herrens mark
Vi var helt på Herrens mark

related.da: at være helt ude at svømme
related.en: to be out of your depth
to be on the right track

sentence.da: Han kan **være på Herrens mark**, når han ikke har læst opgaven.
sentence.en: He can be completely lost when he has not read the assignment.

at være på vej.explanation: "At være på vej" means "to be on the way": Jeg er på vej hjem (I am on my way home). Before a place name, add til (to): Han er på vej til Aarhus (He is on his way to Aarhus).

forms.en: I have been on my way

sentence.da: Vi skal **være på vej** inden otte.
sentence.en: We must be on our way before eight.

at være syg.explanation: "At være syg" means "to be sick" or "to be ill": Jeg er syg (I am sick). To get sick, say at blive syg (to become sick): Jeg bliver syg (I am getting sick).

sentence.da: Jeg har feber og må **være syg** hjemme.
sentence.en: I have a fever and have to stay home sick.

at være træt af.explanation: "At være træt af" means "to be tired of", or fed up with something: Jeg er træt af regnen (I am tired of the rain). For sleepy tired, leave af out: Jeg er træt (I am sleepy).

sentence.da: Man kan let **være træt af** at vente.
sentence.en: You can easily get tired of waiting.

at være ude i god tid.explanation: "At være ude i god tid" means "to be well ahead of time", to start or do something early enough that there is room for delays, so nothing is rushed.

forms.da: Vi er ude i god tid
forms.en: We are well ahead of time

forms.da: Er du ude i god tid?
forms.en: Are you well ahead of time?

forms.da: Man skal være ude i god tid

sentence.da: Vi skal **være ude i god tid**, fordi flyet letter klokken seks.
sentence.en: We must be well ahead of time because the plane takes off at six.

at være uenig.explanation: "At være uenig" means "to disagree" and is the opposite of agreeing: Jeg er uenig med dig (I disagree with you). To disagree about a thing, add i: Vi er uenige i det (We disagree on that).

sentence.da: Det er okay at **være uenig** med en ven.
sentence.en: It is okay to disagree with a friend.

at være vant til.explanation: "At være vant til" means "to be used to", for something you have lived with for a long time: Hun er vant til støjen (She is used to the noise). After til, you can also use at plus a verb: Jeg er vant til at stå tidligt op (I am used to getting up early).

sentence.da: Efter et år vil du **være vant til** kulden.
sentence.en: After a year, you will be used to the cold.

at være ved at.explanation: "At være ved at" means "to be about to" or "to be in the middle of": Toget er ved at køre (The train is about to leave). Jeg er ved at spise (I am in the middle of eating). The situation tells you which one it is.

forms.en: to be about to / be in the middle of
I am about to / am in the middle of
I was about to / was in the middle of
I have been about to / been in the middle of

sentence.da: Han ser ud til at **være ved at** falde i søvn.
sentence.en: He seems to be about to fall asleep.

at være vild med.explanation: "At være vild med" means "to be crazy about", so to like something a lot: Jeg er vild med pizza (I love pizza). It also works for people: Hun er vild med ham (She is crazy about him).

sentence.da: Du vil **være vild med** den her film.
sentence.en: You will love this movie.

at være væk.explanation: "At være væk" means "to be gone" or "to be away". It is used for people who are not there (Han er væk, He is gone) and for things that have disappeared (Min telefon er væk, My phone is gone).

sentence.da: Han skal **være væk** i to dage.
sentence.en: He has to be away for two days.

at værne om.explanation: "At værne om" means "to protect" or "to safeguard", to guard something valuable so that it is kept. The small word om is always there: værne om friheden (protect freedom). It is for things you value and want to keep, more than for guarding against an attack.

sentence.da: Vi bør **værne om** vores natur og vores sprog.
sentence.en: We should protect our nature and our language.

en vaccination.explanation: "En vaccination" means "a vaccination", a shot that protects you from a disease. The shorter en vaccine is the medicine itself.

sentence.da: Børnene får en **vaccination** hos lægen.
sentence.en: The children get a vaccination at the doctor's.

en vaccine.explanation: "En vaccine" means "a vaccine", the injection that protects you from a disease. Mod (against) comes after it: en vaccine mod mæslinger (a vaccine against measles).

sentence.da: Lægen gav mig en **vaccine** mod influenza.
sentence.en: The doctor gave me a vaccine against the flu.

en vaffel.explanation: "En vaffel" means "a waffle", and also the crisp cone that holds ice cream: en is i vaffel (an ice cream in a cone).

sentence.da: Til dessert får jeg en **vaffel** med is.
sentence.en: For dessert I get a waffle with ice cream.

en vagt.explanation: "En vagt" means "a guard", and also "a shift" at work, for example in a hospital: Hun har vagt i weekenden (She is on duty this weekend). A security guard is en sikkerhedsvagt.

sentence.da: Han har **vagt** på hospitalet i nat.
sentence.en: He is on duty at the hospital tonight.

en vagtlæge.explanation: "En vagtlæge" means "an on-call doctor", a doctor you can reach in the evening, at night and on weekends, when your own doctor's office is closed. You usually call lægevagten (the out-of-hours doctor service) to reach one.

sentence.da: Om natten kan du få hjælp fra en **vagtlæge**.
sentence.en: At night you can get help from an on-call doctor.

en valgkamp.explanation: "En valgkamp" means "an election campaign", the weeks before an election when parties try to win votes with speeches and promises. It is valg (election) plus kamp (fight), a fight for votes.

sentence.da: I en **valgkamp** prøver partierne at vinde vælgernes stemmer.
sentence.en: In an election campaign the parties try to win the voters' votes.

en valgkreds.explanation: "En valgkreds" means "a constituency", an area whose voters together elect their own members of parliament. Where you live decides which one you vote in.

sentence.da: Man stemmer i den **valgkreds**, hvor man bor.
sentence.en: You vote in the constituency where you live.

en valgmulighed.explanation: "En valgmulighed" means "an option", one of several things you can choose between, for example on a menu or in the settings of a phone. It is valg (choice) plus mulighed (possibility).

related.en: a decision to leave something out

sentence.da: Der er kun en **valgmulighed**, og det er at vente.
sentence.en: There is only one option, and that is to wait.

en valnød.explanation: "En valnød" means "a walnut", a nut with a wrinkled inside that people often eat in cakes and salads. It grows on a big tree and has a hard shell.

sentence.da: Jeg knækker en **valnød** og spiser den.
sentence.en: I crack a walnut and eat it.

en valuta.explanation: "En valuta" means "a currency", the kind of money a country uses, such as kroner or euro. Money from another country is udenlandsk valuta (foreign currency).

sentence.da: Euro er den **valuta**, de bruger i Tyskland.
sentence.en: The euro is the currency they use in Germany.

en vampyr.explanation: "En vampyr" means "a vampire", a creature in scary stories that drinks blood. Danish spells it with a y, where English has an i.

sentence.da: En **vampyr** drikker blod og sover om dagen.
sentence.en: A vampire drinks blood and sleeps during the day.

en vandflaske.explanation: "En vandflaske" means "a water bottle", the bottle you refill and carry with you. It is built from vand (water) and flaske (bottle).

sentence.da: Jeg fylder min **vandflaske** med koldt vand.
sentence.en: I fill my water bottle with cold water.

en vandhane.explanation: "En vandhane" means "a faucet" or "a tap". It is built from vand (water) and hane (a tap or a rooster): Luk for vandhanen (Turn off the faucet).

sentence.da: Der drypper vand fra en **vandhane** i køkkenet.
sentence.en: Water is dripping from a faucet in the kitchen.

en vandkande.explanation: "En vandkande" means "a watering can". It is built from vand (water) and kande (jug), the same kande as in en kaffekande (a coffee pot).

sentence.da: Jeg vander blomsterne med en **vandkande**.
sentence.en: I water the flowers with a watering can.

en vandkaraffel.explanation: "En vandkaraffel" means "a water carafe", a container for serving water at the table.

sentence.da: Der står en **vandkaraffel** på bordet.
sentence.en: There is a water carafe on the table.

en vandmand.explanation: "En vandmand" means "a jellyfish", a soft sea animal that can sting you if you touch it. The word is literally "water man", and with a capital V, Vandmanden is also the zodiac sign Aquarius.

sentence.da: Hvis du rører en **vandmand**, kan den brænde dig.
sentence.en: If you touch a jellyfish, it can burn you.

en vandmelon.explanation: "En vandmelon" means "a watermelon", built from vand (water) and melon. It is big, red inside, and full of water.

sentence.da: På en varm dag spiser vi **vandmelon**.
sentence.en: On a warm day, we eat watermelon.

en vandpyt.explanation: "En vandpyt" means "a puddle", water that stays on the ground after rain.

sentence.da: Jeg trådte i en stor **vandpyt** og blev våd.
sentence.en: I stepped in a big puddle and got wet.

en vandregning.explanation: "En vandregning" means "a water bill". It is vand (water) plus regning (bill), which also means the check at a restaurant: Regningen, tak (The check, please).

sentence.da: Vi sparer på vandet og får en lav **vandregning**.
sentence.en: We save on water and get a low water bill.

en vandretur.explanation: "En vandretur" means "a hike", a long walk in nature. It is built from at vandre (to hike) and tur (trip), the same tur as in en cykeltur (a bike ride).

sentence.da: Vi tager på en lang **vandretur** i weekenden.
sentence.en: We are going on a long hike this weekend.

en vane.explanation: "En vane" means "a habit", something you do again and again without thinking. To say what you usually do, use for vane (as a habit): Jeg har for vane at gå en tur (I usually take a walk).

sentence.da: Det er en dårlig **vane** at komme for sent.
sentence.en: It is a bad habit to be late.

en vaniljekrans.explanation: "En vaniljekrans" means "a vanilla butter cookie", a traditional Danish cookie that many families bake at Christmas. It is built from vanilje (vanilla) and krans (a wreath).

sentence.da: En **vaniljekrans** er en lille, sprød ring af smør, mel og sukker.
sentence.en: A vanilla butter cookie is a small, crisp ring of butter, flour and sugar.

en vanskelighed.explanation: "En vanskelighed" means "a difficulty", something that makes a task hard to do. It is often used in the plural: Hun har vanskeligheder med at høre (She has difficulty hearing).

sentence.da: Den største **vanskelighed** er, at vi mangler tid.
sentence.en: The biggest difficulty is that we are short of time.

en vante.explanation: "En vante" means "a mitten", a warm hand cover with room for the thumb and one shared space for the other fingers. One with a space for each finger is en handske (a glove).

sentence.da: Jeg har mistet min ene **vante**, så min hånd fryser.
sentence.en: I have lost one of my mittens, so my hand is freezing.

en vare.explanation: "En vare" means "an item" or "a product" that is for sale. For a thing you own, say en ting (a thing) instead.

sentence.da: Denne **vare** koster kun tyve kroner.
sentence.en: This item costs only twenty kroner.

en varedeklaration.explanation: "En varedeklaration" means "a product label", the printed information on a food or other product about what is inside, how much there is and who made it. Food has to carry one.

sentence.da: Der står på en **varedeklaration**, hvad en vare indeholder.
sentence.en: A product label says what a product contains.

en vareprøve.explanation: "En vareprøve" means "a product sample", a small free amount to try at home.

sentence.da: Jeg fik en **vareprøve** af den nye creme.
sentence.en: I got a product sample of the new cream.

en varevogn.explanation: "En varevogn" means "a van", a vehicle for carrying goods. It is built from varer (goods) and vogn (wagon), the same vogn as in en indkøbsvogn (a shopping cart).

sentence.da: Vi flytter vores møbler i en **varevogn**.
sentence.en: We are moving our furniture in a van.

en variation.explanation: "En variation" means "a variation", a different form of something, or a change that keeps things from being the same every time. Use over for what is varied: en variation over en gammel opskrift (a variation on an old recipe).

sentence.da: Det er sundt med **variation** i det, man spiser.
sentence.en: It is healthy to have variation in what you eat.

en varmebølge.explanation: "En varmebølge" means "a heatwave", several days in a row of very hot weather. It is varme (heat) plus bølge (wave). Another word with the same meaning is en hedebølge.

sentence.da: Under en **varmebølge** bør man drikke meget vand.
sentence.en: During a heatwave you should drink a lot of water.

en varmepumpe.explanation: "En varmepumpe" means "a heat pump". It is built from varme (heat) and pumpe (pump), and it takes heat from the air or the ground to warm a house.

sentence.da: Vi varmer huset op med en **varmepumpe**.
sentence.en: We heat the house with a heat pump.

en varmerekord.explanation: "En varmerekord" means "a heat record", the highest temperature ever measured in a place or in a certain month. For the lowest temperature, use en kulderekord (a cold record).

sentence.da: I dag blev der sat en ny **varmerekord** i Danmark.
sentence.en: Today a new heat record was set in Denmark.

en vase.explanation: "En vase" means "a vase", for cut flowers.

sentence.da: Hun sætter blomsterne i en **vase** med vand.
sentence.en: She puts the flowers in a vase with water.

en vask.explanation: "En vask" means "a sink", in the bathroom or the kitchen. The word at vaske (to wash) looks almost the same but is an action: Jeg vasker hænder (I wash my hands).

sentence.da: Vi har en stor **vask** i køkkenet.
sentence.en: We have a big sink in the kitchen.

en vaskekælder.explanation: "En vaskekælder" means "a laundry room" in the basement of a building. It is built from vaske (to wash) and kælder (basement). Many Danish apartment buildings have one that all the residents use.

sentence.da: Vores tøj vaskes i en **vaskekælder** under huset.
sentence.en: Our clothes are washed in a laundry room under the house.

en vaskemaskine.explanation: "En vaskemaskine" means "a washing machine", the machine that cleans clothes with water and soap.

sentence.da: Jeg vasker tøj i en **vaskemaskine**.
sentence.en: I wash clothes in a washing machine.

en vatpind.explanation: "En vatpind" means "a cotton swab". It is built from vat (cotton wool) and en pind (a stick), so it is a small stick with cotton on the end. The same pind is in en spisepind (a chopstick).

sentence.da: Hun tager makeup af med en **vatpind**.
sentence.en: She takes off makeup with a cotton swab.

en vedhæftet fil.explanation: "En vedhæftet fil" means "an attachment", a file sent along with an email, such as a photo or a contract. It is literally "an attached file". In emails you often read Se vedhæftede filer (See the attached files).

sentence.da: Jeg sender dig en **vedhæftet fil** med billederne fra turen.
sentence.en: I am sending you an attachment with the pictures from the trip.

en veganer.explanation: "En veganer" means "a vegan", a person who eats no meat, fish, eggs or dairy. It is different from a vegetarian, who may still eat eggs and dairy.

sentence.da: Hun er **veganer** og spiser hverken kød eller ost.
sentence.en: She is a vegan and eats neither meat nor cheese.

en vegetar.explanation: "En vegetar" means "a vegetarian", a person who does not eat meat. For food, use vegetarisk (vegetarian), as in en vegetarisk ret (a vegetarian dish).

sentence.da: En **vegetar** spiser ikke kød.
sentence.en: A vegetarian does not eat meat.

en vej.explanation: "En vej" means "a road" and also "a way" or route: Hvilken vej skal jeg gå? means "Which way should I go?". At spørge om vej means "to ask for directions", with no en before vej.

sentence.da: Bilen kører på en lang **vej**.
sentence.en: The car drives on a long road.

en vejleder.explanation: "En vejleder" means "a supervisor", someone who guides you in your studies or work and gives feedback. It comes from at vejlede (to guide).

sentence.da: Min **vejleder** læser mit speciale og siger, hvad jeg kan forbedre.
sentence.en: My supervisor reads my thesis and says what I can improve.

en vejledning.explanation: "En vejledning" means "a guide / guidance", help or instructions that show you how to do something. A person who gives guidance is en vejleder (an advisor).

sentence.da: Du kan finde en **vejledning** på hjemmesiden.
sentence.en: You can find a guide on the website.

en vejrmelding.explanation: "En vejrmelding" means "a weather report". It is built from vejr (weather) and melding (message), the same melding as in en fejlmelding (an error message).

sentence.da: Jeg lytter til en **vejrmelding** om regn i morgen.
sentence.en: I listen to a weather report about rain tomorrow.

en vejrudsigt.explanation: "En vejrudsigt" means "a weather forecast", a description of what the weather will be like. It is made from vejr (weather) and udsigt (outlook), which on its own also means a view: Der er en flot udsigt (There is a great view).

sentence.da: Jeg ser en **vejrudsigt** om regn i morgen.
sentence.en: I see a weather forecast about rain tomorrow.

en vejviser.explanation: "En vejviser" means "a signpost", something that shows the way, and it is also a printed directory of addresses. It is built from vej (road) and viser (a pointer, from at vise, to show).

sentence.da: Ved krydset viser en **vejviser**, hvilken vej vi skal gå.
sentence.en: At the crossing a signpost shows which way we must go.

en vekselkurs.explanation: "En vekselkurs" means "an exchange rate", the price of one country's money in another's, such as how many kroner you get for one euro. The rate changes every day.

sentence.da: Hvad er den aktuelle **vekselkurs** mellem kroner og euro?
sentence.en: What is the current exchange rate between kroner and euros?

en velsignelse.explanation: "En velsignelse" means "a blessing", both a religious one from God and, in everyday speech, something that is a great help: Regnen er en velsignelse for bønderne (The rain is a blessing for the farmers).

sentence.da: Præsten gav parret sin **velsignelse** efter brylluppet.
sentence.en: The priest gave the couple his blessing after the wedding.

en ven.explanation: "En ven" means "a friend", usually a male friend, but it is also used for a friend of either sex: Hun er min bedste ven (She is my best friend). Be careful with kæreste (boyfriend or girlfriend): it means a romantic partner, not just a friend.

sentence.da: Jeg spiller fodbold med min **ven**.
sentence.en: I play soccer with my friend.

en veninde.explanation: "En veninde" means "a female friend", used when the friend is a woman or girl. For a male friend, or a friend in general, use en ven (a friend).

sentence.da: Hun er min **veninde**, ikke min kæreste.
sentence.en: She is my female friend, not my girlfriend.

en vennegruppe.explanation: "En vennegruppe" means "a group of friends", built from venner (friends) and gruppe (group), the same gruppe as in en studiegruppe (a study group).

sentence.da: Min **vennegruppe** mødes hver fredag.
sentence.en: My group of friends meets every Friday.

en venteliste.explanation: "En venteliste" means "a waiting list": the list you are put on when something is full.

sentence.da: Vi står på **venteliste** til en plads i børnehaven.
sentence.en: We are on the waiting list for a spot in kindergarten.

en ventetid.explanation: "En ventetid" means "a wait time", how long you wait for something. It is built from at vente (to wait) and en tid (a time). You ask about it with Hvad er ventetiden? (How long is the wait?)

sentence.da: Der er lang **ventetid** hos lægen.
sentence.en: There is a long wait at the doctor.

en ventilator.explanation: "En ventilator" means "a fan" that moves air. A fan of a team or a singer is en fan, not en ventilator.

sentence.da: Det er varmt, og jeg tænder en **ventilator**.
sentence.en: It is hot, and I am turning on a fan.

en verden.explanation: "En verden" means "a world". Common phrases are i hele verden (all over the world) and verdens bedste (the best in the world), where verdens means "the world's".

sentence.da: Jeg vil rejse rundt i **verden**.
sentence.en: I want to travel around the world.

en verdensdel.explanation: "En verdensdel" means "a continent", one of the very large parts of the Earth, such as Asia or Africa. It is literally "world part". The word et kontinent also exists and means the same.

sentence.da: Europa er den **verdensdel**, hvor Danmark ligger.
sentence.en: Europe is the continent where Denmark is located.

en verdenskrig.explanation: "En verdenskrig" means "a world war". There were two: første verdenskrig (the First World War, 1914 to 1918) and anden verdenskrig (the Second World War, 1939 to 1945).

sentence.da: Min oldefar var soldat under den første **verdenskrig**.
sentence.en: My great-grandfather was a soldier during the first world war.

en version.explanation: "En version" means "a version", one form of something. It can also mean one person's account of what happened: Hun fortalte sin version (She told her version).

sentence.da: Filmen findes i en dansk **version**.
sentence.en: The film exists in a Danish version.

en vest.explanation: "En vest" means "a vest", a piece of clothing without sleeves, often worn over a shirt.

sentence.da: Min onkel har en grå **vest** over skjorten.
sentence.en: My uncle has a gray vest over his shirt.

en veteran.explanation: "En veteran" means "a veteran", most often a former member of the armed forces, especially one who served abroad. It also means a very experienced person in a field. Before another word it means old and well kept: en veteranbil (a vintage car).

sentence.da: Han er **veteran** efter mange år i hæren.
sentence.en: He is a veteran after many years in the army.

en vicepræsident.explanation: "En vicepræsident" means "a vice president", the person ranking just below a president, who takes over if the president cannot do the job. Denmark has a king or queen instead of a president, so the word is mostly used about other countries and about organizations.

sentence.da: En **vicepræsident** kan overtage, hvis præsidenten bliver syg.
sentence.en: A vice president can take over if the president gets sick.

en vicevært.explanation: "En vicevært" means "a caretaker" or "a janitor", the person who looks after an apartment building, for example by cleaning, fixing small things and keeping the yard tidy. Today the job title is sometimes en ejendomsfunktionær (property worker).

sentence.da: Når lyset i trappen er i stykker, ringer vi til en **vicevært**.
sentence.en: When the light on the stairs is broken, we call a caretaker.

en videnskab.explanation: "En videnskab" means "a science", a field of knowledge built by study and tests, such as physics or chemistry. For the school subject science, Danes say naturfag.

sentence.da: Biologi er en **videnskab**, der studerer alt levende.
sentence.en: Biology is a science that studies everything living.

en videnskabsmand.explanation: "En videnskabsmand" means "a scientist". It is built from videnskab (science) and mand (man), a pattern also used in en brandmand (a firefighter).

sentence.da: Den kendte **videnskabsmand** arbejder på et laboratorium.
sentence.en: The famous scientist works at a laboratory.

en video.explanation: "En video" means "a video", a short or long film you watch online. To make one, say at optage en video (to record a video).

sentence.da: Jeg har set en sjov **video** på nettet.
sentence.en: I watched a funny video online.

en vielsesring.explanation: "En vielsesring" means "a wedding ring", the ring a married person wears. Do not mix it up with en forlovelsesring (an engagement ring).

sentence.da: Han har en **vielsesring** på fingeren.
sentence.en: He has a wedding ring on his finger.

en vikar.explanation: "En vikar" means "a substitute teacher", someone who steps in when the regular teacher is away. It also works for other jobs: en vikar på kontoret (a temp at the office).

sentence.da: Vi får en **vikar**, fordi vores lærer er syg.
sentence.en: We get a substitute because our teacher is sick.

en viking.explanation: "En viking" means "a Viking", a Scandinavian sailor-warrior from long ago.

sentence.da: En **viking** sejlede over havet i et langt skib.
sentence.en: A Viking sailed over the sea in a long ship.

en vilje.explanation: "En vilje" means "a will", the drive to want something. It is also in a saying: Hvor der er en vilje, er der en vej (Where there is a will, there is a way).

sentence.da: Det kræver **vilje** at holde op med at ryge.
sentence.en: It takes willpower to quit smoking.

en villa.explanation: "En villa" means "a detached house", a house that stands alone with its own garden. Unlike the English word "villa", it does not have to be fancy: it is an ordinary family house.

sentence.da: De bor i en stor **villa** med have.
sentence.en: They live in a big detached house with a garden.

en vin.explanation: "En vin" means "a wine". You can name the color: en rødvin (a red wine) or en hvidvin (a white wine). To order, say et glas vin (a glass of wine) or en flaske vin (a bottle of wine).

sentence.da: **Vin** er lavet af druer.
sentence.en: Wine is made from grapes.

en vinbar.explanation: "En vinbar" means "a wine bar", a place that serves wine by the glass.

sentence.da: Vi drikker rødvin på en hyggelig **vinbar**.
sentence.en: We drink red wine at a cozy wine bar.

en vinder.explanation: "En vinder" means "a winner", the person or team that wins. The one who loses is en taber (a loser).

sentence.da: Hvem bliver **vinder** af kampen i aften?
sentence.en: Who will be the winner of the match tonight?

en vindmølle.explanation: "En vindmølle" means "a wind turbine" or "a windmill". Danish uses one word for both the old grain mill and the modern machine that makes power from the wind.

sentence.da: Vi kan se en stor **vindmølle** fra vinduet.
sentence.en: We can see a big wind turbine from the window.

en vindrue.explanation: "En vindrue" means "a grape", and en drue (a grape) means the same. The word starts with vin (wine), but these grapes are for eating, not only for making wine.

sentence.da: Han spiser en grøn **vindrue** ad gangen.
sentence.en: He eats one green grape at a time.

en vindueskarm.explanation: "En vindueskarm" means "a windowsill", the flat ledge at the bottom of a window. Danish says i (in) for it: Katten sidder i vindueskarmen (The cat sits on the windowsill).

sentence.da: Der står en lille plante i hver **vindueskarm**.
sentence.en: There is a small plant on every windowsill.

en vinduesplads.explanation: "En vinduesplads" means "a window seat" on a plane, bus or train. Its opposite is en gangplads (an aisle seat).

sentence.da: Fra en **vinduesplads** kan man se skyerne.
sentence.en: From a window seat you can see the clouds.

en vinduespudsning.explanation: "En vinduespudsning" means "a window cleaning", the job of cleaning windows, yourself or as a paid service. It comes from at pudse (to polish), which Danes use for windows and also for shining shoes: at pudse sko (to polish shoes).

sentence.da: Vi har bestilt en **vinduespudsning**, fordi vinduerne er meget snavsede.
sentence.en: We have ordered a window cleaning because the windows are very dirty.

en vinduesvisker.explanation: "En vinduesvisker" means "a windshield wiper". It is vindue (window) plus visker (wiper), the arm on a car that sweeps rain off the glass.

sentence.da: Det regner meget, og min **vinduesvisker** går hurtigt.
sentence.en: It is raining a lot, and my wiper moves fast.

en vinge.explanation: "En vinge" means "a wing", what a bird or insect has on its body, and also what holds up a plane or turns on a windmill. For the wing of a building or a political side, Danes use en fløj.

sentence.da: Fuglen kan ikke flyve, fordi den har brækket en **vinge**.
sentence.en: The bird cannot fly because it has broken a wing.

en vinhandel.explanation: "En vinhandel" means "a wine shop", a shop that mainly sells wine and often other drinks. Handel (trade) works the same way in other shop words, such as en blomsterhandel (a flower shop).

sentence.da: Du kan få hjælp til at vælge en god rødvin i en **vinhandel**.
sentence.en: You can get help choosing a good red wine in a wine shop.

en vinkel.explanation: "En vinkel" means "an angle", in math and also in how you look at things: Jeg ser det fra en anden vinkel (I see it from another angle).

sentence.da: Her er en **vinkel** på halvfems grader.
sentence.en: Here is an angle of ninety degrees.

en vinliste.explanation: "En vinliste" means "a wine list", the list of wines a restaurant serves. It is built from vin (wine) and liste (list), the same liste as in en gæsteliste (a guest list).

sentence.da: På en **vinliste** står mange slags vin.
sentence.en: A wine list shows many kinds of wine.

en vinter.explanation: "En vinter" means "a winter". Use om vinteren (in the winter) for winters in general, and i vinter (this winter) for the current one.

sentence.da: En **vinter** i Danmark er kold og mørk.
sentence.en: A winter in Denmark is cold and dark.

en vinterbader.explanation: "En vinterbader" means "a winter swimmer", a person who swims outdoors in the cold months. It is built from vinter (winter) and at bade (to take a dip), the Danish word for going into the sea or a lake, not for washing.

sentence.da: Min nabo er **vinterbader** og svømmer i havet hver morgen.
sentence.en: My neighbor is a winter swimmer and swims in the sea every morning.

en vinterdag.explanation: "En vinterdag" means "a winter day". It is built from vinter (winter) and dag (day), and the same vinter is in en vinterferie (a winter break).

sentence.da: På en **vinterdag** er det mørkt klokken fire.
sentence.en: On a winter day it is dark at four o'clock.

en vinterferie.explanation: "En vinterferie" means "a winter break", a short holiday in the cold season. In Denmark it is a week in February, and many families use it to go skiing.

sentence.da: I en **vinterferie** har børnene fri fra skole i en uge.
sentence.en: During a winter break the children are off from school for a week.

en vinterjakke.explanation: "En vinterjakke" means "a winter jacket", a thick, warm jacket for cold weather. It is made from vinter (winter) and jakke (jacket), the same jakke as in en læderjakke (a leather jacket).

sentence.da: I sneen har jeg en **vinterjakke** på.
sentence.en: In the snow I wear a winter jacket.

en vinternat.explanation: "En vinternat" means "a winter night". It is built from vinter (winter) and nat (night). Nat also appears in i nat (last night or tonight): Jeg sov dårligt i nat (I slept badly last night).

sentence.da: Det er koldt og mørkt på en **vinternat**.
sentence.en: It is cold and dark on a winter night.

en vinterstøvle.explanation: "En vinterstøvle" means "a winter boot", a warm boot for snow and cold. You usually say it in the plural: Jeg tager vinterstøvler på (I put on winter boots).

sentence.da: Min venstre **vinterstøvle** er våd af sne.
sentence.en: My left winter boot is wet from snow.

en violin.explanation: "En violin" means "a violin". Danish also has en fiol (a fiddle), often used for folk music: Han spiller fiol til dans (He plays fiddle for dancing).

sentence.da: Min datter øver sig på **violin** hver dag.
sentence.en: My daughter practices the violin every day.

en vippe.explanation: "En vippe" means "a seesaw", the long board that two children sit on, one at each end, going up and down. The same word is in en øjenvippe (an eyelash), from at vippe (to tip up and down).

sentence.da: To børn sidder på hver sin ende af en **vippe**.
sentence.en: Two children sit at each end of a seesaw.

en virkelighed.explanation: "En virkelighed" means "a reality", what is real, as opposed to what you imagine: Drømmen blev til virkelighed (The dream became reality).

sentence.da: Eventyret er en historie, ikke **virkelighed**.
sentence.en: The fairy tale is a story, not reality.

en virkning.explanation: "En virkning" means "an effect", the result that something has on something else, especially from a medicine or a law. With bi- (by) in front, it is en bivirkning (a side effect).

sentence.da: Den nye lov fik en stor **virkning** på priserne.
sentence.en: The new law had a big effect on prices.

en virksomhed.explanation: "En virksomhed" means "a business", seen as an organization with workers.

sentence.da: Hun driver en lille **virksomhed** med fem ansatte.
sentence.en: She runs a small business with five employees.

en virus.explanation: "En virus" means "a virus", both for illness and for computers: Min computer har fået en virus (My computer has caught a virus). Jeg har en virus (I have a virus) means you are sick.

sentence.da: Min computer har fået en **virus** fra en e-mail.
sentence.en: My computer got a virus from an email.

en vision.explanation: "En vision" means "a vision", a clear picture of how you want the future to be, for a company, a city or yourself. It is not about eyesight. For that, use syn (sight).

sentence.da: Firmaets **vision** er, at alle børn kan lære at læse.
sentence.en: The company's vision is that all children can learn to read.

en vissen blomst.explanation: "En vissen blomst" means "a withered flower", one that has dried up and drooped. The describing word changes with the thing: et vissent blad (a withered leaf), visne blomster (withered flowers).

sentence.da: Uden vand bliver en blomst til en **vissen blomst**.
sentence.en: Without water, a flower turns into a withered flower.

en vitamin.explanation: "En vitamin" means "a vitamin". A named one puts the letter first: C-vitamin (vitamin C).

sentence.da: Hun tager en **vitamin** hver morgen.
sentence.en: She takes a vitamin every morning.

en vits.explanation: "En vits" means "a joke", a short funny story with a punchline. The surprise at the end is called en pointe (a punchline).

sentence.da: Hun fortæller en **vits**, og alle griner.
sentence.en: She tells a joke, and everyone laughs.

en vittighed.explanation: "En vittighed" means "a joke". It is the same as en vits (a joke), so you can use either one.

sentence.da: Alle grinede af hans **vittighed**.
sentence.en: Everyone laughed at his joke.

en vogn.explanation: "En vogn" means "a wagon" or "a cart", a vehicle on wheels that carries things: Maden står på en vogn (The food is on a cart).

sentence.da: Hesten trækker en tung **vogn** op ad bakken.
sentence.en: The horse pulls a heavy wagon up the hill.

en vokal.explanation: "En vokal" means "a vowel", a speech sound made with the mouth open and nothing blocking the air. Danish has nine in writing: a, e, i, o, u, y, æ, ø and å.

sentence.da: Ordet bil har kun en **vokal**, nemlig i.
sentence.en: The word bil has only one vowel, namely i.

en voksen.explanation: "En voksen" means "an adult". The word comes from at vokse (to grow), so it is someone who has grown up.

sentence.da: Et barn bliver til en **voksen**.
sentence.en: A child becomes an adult.

en vorte.explanation: "En vorte" means "a wart", a small hard bump on the skin, often on a hand or foot, caused by a virus. It is harmless and often goes away by itself.

sentence.da: Jeg har fået en **vorte** på fingeren, men den gør ikke ondt.
sentence.en: I have got a wart on my finger, but it does not hurt.

en vugge.explanation: "En vugge" means "a cradle", a small bed for a baby that rocks. The same word is the verb at vugge (to rock).

sentence.da: Den lille baby sover i en **vugge** ved sengen.
sentence.en: The little baby sleeps in a cradle next to the bed.

en vuggestue.explanation: "En vuggestue" means "a nursery", a daycare place for the youngest children, from about six months to about three years. From around three until school, children go to en børnehave (a kindergarten).

sentence.da: Vores datter går i **vuggestue**, mens vi er på arbejde.
sentence.en: Our daughter goes to a nursery while we are at work.

en vulkan.explanation: "En vulkan" means "a volcano". An eruption is et vulkanudbrud (a volcanic eruption).

sentence.da: Der kommer varm lava ud af en **vulkan**.
sentence.en: Hot lava comes out of a volcano.

en vurdering.explanation: "En vurdering" means "an assessment", a judgment of how good, valuable or serious something is, made after thinking it over. It is used for a teacher's view of a pupil, for the price of a house and for a risk.

sentence.da: Lægens **vurdering** er, at du skal hvile i en uge.
sentence.en: The doctor's assessment is that you should rest for a week.

en våbenhvile.explanation: "En våbenhvile" means "a ceasefire", an agreement to stop the fighting for a time or for good. It is built from våben (weapon) and hvile (rest).

sentence.da: Landene indgik en **våbenhvile**, og kampene stoppede.
sentence.en: The countries made a ceasefire, and the fighting stopped.

en vædder.explanation: "En vædder" means "a ram", a male sheep, often with big curved horns. With a capital V, Væderen is also the zodiac sign Aries.

sentence.da: Den store **vædder** med krumme horn står på marken.
sentence.en: The big ram with curved horns is standing in the field.

en væg.explanation: "En væg" means "a wall" inside a building or room. For a wall outdoors, such as around a garden, Danes say en mur (a brick or stone wall).

sentence.da: Billedet hænger på en **væg**.
sentence.en: The picture hangs on a wall.

en vægt.explanation: "En vægt" means "a weight": Hvad er din vægt? (What is your weight?) It is also the machine you stand on to weigh yourself, a scale: Vægten står på badeværelset (The scale is in the bathroom).

sentence.da: Kufferten har en **vægt** på tyve kilo.
sentence.en: The suitcase has a weight of twenty kilos.

en vælger.explanation: "En vælger" means "a voter", a person who may take part in an election by choosing who should govern. It comes from at vælge (to choose).

sentence.da: Hver **vælger** lægger sin stemme i urnen.
sentence.en: Each voter puts their vote in the ballot box.

en værdi.explanation: "En værdi" means "a value", how much something is worth in money or importance. In the plural, værdier also means the things a person finds important, such as honesty and freedom.

sentence.da: Billedet har stor **værdi**, fordi det er meget gammelt.
sentence.en: The picture has great value because it is very old.

en vært.explanation: "En vært" means "a host", the person who has people over to their home. It also means the host of a show: Hun er vært på et tv-program (She is the host of a TV show).

sentence.da: Vores **vært** tog imod os ved døren.
sentence.en: Our host welcomed us at the door.

en værtinde.explanation: "En værtinde" means "a hostess", a woman who welcomes people to her home or an event and looks after them. The man is en vært (a host).

sentence.da: Som **værtinde** skal hun sørge for, at gæsterne har det godt.
sentence.en: As hostess she must make sure the guests are doing well.

en værtindegave.explanation: "En værtindegave" means "a hostess gift", a small present you bring when you are invited to dinner. It is built from værtinde (hostess) and gave (gift).

sentence.da: Jeg tog blomster med som **værtindegave**.
sentence.en: I brought flowers as a hostess gift.

en væske.explanation: "En væske" means "a liquid" or "a fluid", something that flows, like water or milk. Doctors also use it for what you drink: Drik meget væske (Drink a lot of fluids).

sentence.da: Vand er en **væske**, men is er fast.
sentence.en: Water is a liquid, but ice is solid.

et valg.explanation: "Et valg" means "a choice" and also "an election": Det er dit valg (It is your choice). Der er valg i år (There is an election this year).

sentence.da: Du har et **valg**: te eller kaffe?
sentence.en: You have a choice: tea or coffee?

et vandfald.explanation: "Et vandfald" means "a waterfall". It is built from vand (water) and fald (a fall). Et fald is also a drop in numbers: et fald i prisen (a fall in the price).

sentence.da: Vandet falder ned fra et højt **vandfald**.
sentence.en: The water falls down from a tall waterfall.

et vandland.explanation: "Et vandland" means "a water park", a place with pools, waves and many things to play on. The name is simply vand (water) plus land (land): a land of water.

sentence.da: Vi tog børnene med til et **vandland**, hvor de kunne bade hele dagen.
sentence.en: We took the children to a water park where they could swim all day.

et vandrerhjem.explanation: "Et vandrerhjem" means "a hostel", a cheap place to stay. It is built from vandrer (hiker) and hjem (home), so literally a hiker's home. Hjem also ends et plejehjem (a nursing home).

sentence.da: Vi bor billigt på et **vandrerhjem**.
sentence.en: We stay cheaply at a hostel.

et vareudvalg.explanation: "Et vareudvalg" means "a range of goods", how many different things a shop offers.

sentence.da: Butikken har et stort **vareudvalg** og lave priser.
sentence.en: The store has a large range of goods and low prices.

et varsel.explanation: "Et varsel" means "a notice" or "a warning" given before something happens: et varsel om storm (a storm warning). It is also used at work for advance notice of an action: et varsel om strejke (a strike notice).

sentence.da: Vi fik kun en uges **varsel** om flytningen.
sentence.en: We got only a week's notice about the move.

et vaskemærke.explanation: "Et vaskemærke" means "a care label", the tag in clothes that says how to wash them. It is built from vaske (wash) and mærke (label). Et mærke also means a brand: et kendt mærke (a famous brand).

sentence.da: Der står 30 grader på det lille **vaskemærke**.
sentence.en: It says 30 degrees on the little care label.

et vaskeri.explanation: "Et vaskeri" means "a laundromat", a place outside your home where you wash clothes. A laundry room inside your own building is et fællesvaskeri (a shared laundry room).

sentence.da: Jeg har ingen vaskemaskine og vasker på et **vaskeri**.
sentence.en: I have no washing machine and wash at a laundromat.

et vaskerum.explanation: "Et vaskerum" means "a laundry room", a room for washing clothes, often shared in an apartment building.

sentence.da: Vi har et fælles **vaskerum** i kælderen.
sentence.en: We have a shared laundry room in the basement.

et vejskilt.explanation: "Et vejskilt" means "a road sign", the kind that shows a direction or a speed limit. It is built from vej (road) and skilt (sign). Et skilt is any sign with writing: et skilt på døren (a sign on the door).

sentence.da: På et **vejskilt** står der 50 kilometer til Aarhus.
sentence.en: On a road sign it says 50 kilometers to Aarhus.

et vendepunkt.explanation: "Et vendepunkt" means "a turning point", the moment when things start going in a new direction. It is built from at vende (to turn) and et punkt (a point), and it is used for a match, a story or a life: et vendepunkt i kampen (a turning point in the match).

sentence.da: Den dag blev et **vendepunkt** i hendes liv.
sentence.en: That day became a turning point in her life.

et venskab.explanation: "Et venskab" means "a friendship". It is built from ven (friend). The ending -skab also makes et fællesskab (a community) and et ægteskab (a marriage).

sentence.da: Deres **venskab** har holdt i mange år.
sentence.en: Their friendship has lasted for many years.

et venteværelse.explanation: "Et venteværelse" means "a waiting room". It is built from at vente (to wait) and et værelse (a room). Et værelse is also a bedroom or hotel room: et dobbeltværelse (a double room).

sentence.da: Vi venter på lægen i et **venteværelse**.
sentence.en: We wait for the doctor in a waiting room.

et verdenshav.explanation: "Et verdenshav" means "an ocean", one of the huge bodies of water that cover the earth. The everyday word is et hav (a sea or ocean), and verdenshav is used when talking about the oceans of the whole world, like Stillehavet (the Pacific).

sentence.da: Atlanterhavet er et stort **verdenshav** mellem Europa og Amerika.
sentence.en: The Atlantic is a big ocean between Europe and America.

et vers.explanation: "Et vers" means "a verse", a group of lines in a poem or song. Without et, it means poetry in general: Han skriver vers (He writes poetry).

sentence.da: Sangen har tre **vers**, og vi kan alle synge dem.
sentence.en: The song has three verses, and we can all sing them.

et videoopkald.explanation: "Et videoopkald" means "a video call". It is built from video (video) and opkald (call). Et opkald also works for an ordinary phone call: et opkald fra min mor (a call from my mom).

sentence.da: Jeg ser min mormor i et **videoopkald** hver søndag.
sentence.en: I see my grandmother in a video call every Sunday.

et vidne.explanation: "Et vidne" means "a witness", someone who saw what happened. A witness is a person, while et bevis (a piece of evidence) is a thing.

sentence.da: Et **vidne** så bilen køre væk.
sentence.en: A witness saw the car drive away.

et vidnesbyrd.explanation: "Et vidnesbyrd" means "a testimony" and also "evidence" that something is true, often with om (of): et vidnesbyrd om hendes mod (evidence of her courage). For what a person tells the police or a court, Danes more often say et vidneudsagn (a witness statement).

sentence.da: Den gamle kirke er et **vidnesbyrd** om byens historie.
sentence.en: The old church is a testimony to the history of the town.

et vidneudsagn.explanation: "Et vidneudsagn" means "a testimony", what a person who saw something tells the police or a court. It is made of vidne (a witness) and udsagn (a statement).

sentence.da: Politiet har brug for dit **vidneudsagn** om ulykken.
sentence.en: The police need your testimony about the accident.

et vilkår.explanation: "Et vilkår" means "a term", something you must accept in an agreement. It is mostly used in the plural: Læs vilkårene først (Read the terms first). It also means the circumstances someone lives or works under: Det er svære vilkår at arbejde under (These are difficult circumstances to work under).

sentence.da: Et **vilkår** i kontrakten er, at du møder til tiden.
sentence.en: One term in the contract is that you show up on time.

et vindue.explanation: "Et vindue" means "a window", the glass opening in a wall that lets in light. It is also the word for a window on a computer: åbn et nyt vindue (open a new window).

sentence.da: Solen skinner ind gennem et **vindue**.
sentence.en: The sun shines in through a window.

et vinglas.explanation: "Et vinglas" means "a wine glass", the glass with a stem used for wine. It is built from vin (wine) and glas (glass). Glas is also the material: en flaske af glas (a bottle made of glass).

sentence.da: Hun hælder rødvin i et **vinglas**.
sentence.en: She pours red wine into a wine glass.

et visitkort.explanation: "Et visitkort" means "a business card", a small card with your name, job and contact details that you give to people you meet through work.

sentence.da: Han gav mig sit **visitkort**, så jeg kunne ringe til ham.
sentence.en: He gave me his business card so that I could call him.

et viskelæder.explanation: "Et viskelæder" means "an eraser", used to rub out pencil marks. The word is built from viske (to wipe) and læder (leather). Læder alone is the material: en jakke af læder (a jacket made of leather).

sentence.da: Jeg bruger et **viskelæder**, når jeg skriver forkert.
sentence.en: I use an eraser when I write something wrong.

et viskestykke.explanation: "Et viskestykke" means "a dish towel", the piece of fabric you use to dry dishes by hand.

sentence.da: Jeg tørrer tallerkenerne af med et **viskestykke**.
sentence.en: I dry the plates with a dish towel.

et visum.explanation: "Et visum" means "a visa", permission to enter or stay in a country. You apply for one with at søge om (to apply for).

sentence.da: Du skal have et **visum** til Kina.
sentence.en: You need a visa for China.

et våben.explanation: "Et våben" means "a weapon", something made to hurt or fight with. It is also used for things that are not physical: Humor er et våben (Humor is a weapon).

sentence.da: En kniv eller en pistol er et **våben**.
sentence.en: A knife or a pistol is a weapon.

et vådområde.explanation: "Et vådområde" means "a wetland", an area such as a marsh, where the ground is soaked and many birds and plants live.

sentence.da: I et **vådområde** er jorden våd det meste af året.
sentence.en: In a wetland, the ground is wet most of the year.

et væddemål.explanation: "Et væddemål" means "a bet", an agreement that the person who is wrong pays or loses something. In everyday speech, Danes often use the verb at vædde (to bet): Jeg vil vædde på, at han kommer for sent (I bet he will be late).

sentence.da: De lavede et **væddemål** om, hvem der vinder kampen.
sentence.en: They made a bet about who will win the match.

et vækkeur.explanation: "Et vækkeur" means "an alarm clock". It is built from at vække (to wake someone) and et ur (a clock). The alarm on a phone is en alarm (an alarm).

sentence.da: Jeg stiller mit **vækkeur** på seks.
sentence.en: I set my alarm clock to six.

et værelse.explanation: "Et værelse" means "a room" in a home or hotel. For room in the sense of free space, say plads (space): Der er plads (There is room).

sentence.da: Jeg har booket et **værelse** til to nætter.
sentence.en: I have booked a room for two nights.

et værk.explanation: "Et værk" means "a work", something a painter, writer or composer has made: Det er et af hans bedste værker (It is one of his best works). It can also mean a place that makes something, as in et stålværk (a steel mill).

sentence.da: Dette **værk** er malet af en kendt kunstner.
sentence.en: This work was painted by a famous artist.

et værksted.explanation: "Et værksted" means "a workshop", and also "a garage" where cars are repaired: Bilen står på værkstedet (The car is at the garage). A garage for parking is en garage (a garage).

sentence.da: Bilen skal repareres på et **værksted**.
sentence.en: The car has to be repaired at a workshop.

et værktøj.explanation: "Et værktøj" means "a tool", something you use to fix or build things. It is also used for tools as a group: Jeg har værktøj i skuret (I have tools in the shed).

sentence.da: En hammer er et nyttigt **værktøj**.
sentence.en: A hammer is a useful tool.

et værn.explanation: "Et værn" means "a defense" or "a safeguard", something that stands between you and harm: et værn mod kriminalitet (a safeguard against crime). In the military, it also means a branch of the armed forces, such as the army or the navy.

sentence.da: Loven er et **værn** mod misbrug af magt.
sentence.en: The law is a safeguard against abuse of power.

et værtshus.explanation: "Et værtshus" means "a pub", a plain, old-style place where regulars drink beer and chat. It is built from en vært (a host or landlord) and et hus (a house).

sentence.da: På et **værtshus** kan man drikke øl og snakke med andre.
sentence.en: In a pub, you can drink beer and talk to others.

et væsen.explanation: "Et væsen" means "a creature" or "a being", a living thing, often a strange or imaginary one. It also means a person's nature or manner: et roligt væsen (a calm manner).

sentence.da: I eventyret bor der et **væsen** med vinger i skoven.
sentence.en: In the fairy tale, a creature with wings lives in the forest.

et væv.explanation: "Et væv" means "a tissue", the material the body is built from, such as muscle or skin. It also means woven cloth, from at væve (to weave).

sentence.da: Kroppen består af mange slags **væv**, som alle har hver sin opgave.
sentence.en: The body is made of many kinds of tissue, which each have their own job.

vand.explanation: "Vand" means "water". For water in general, you do not need a word for "a": Jeg drikker vand (I drink water).

sentence.da: Fisk lever i **vand**.
sentence.en: Fish live in water.

vanilje.explanation: "Vanilje" means "vanilla", a sweet taste used in cakes and desserts. It starts many food words, such as vaniljeis (vanilla ice cream).

sentence.da: Kagen smager af **vanilje**.
sentence.en: The cake tastes of vanilla.

vanskelig.explanation: "Vanskelig" means "difficult" and describes tasks, questions and situations. Svær (hard) means nearly the same and is more common in everyday speech: Opgaven er svær (The task is hard).

sentence.da: Eksamen var **vanskelig**, men jeg bestod.
sentence.en: The exam was difficult, but I passed.

vant til.explanation: "Vant til" means "used to" in the sense of "accustomed to": Jeg er vant til kulden (I am used to the cold). For a past habit, use plejede at: Jeg plejede at bo i Aarhus (I used to live in Aarhus).

forms.da: Jeg er vant til at stå tidligt op.
forms.en: I am used to getting up early.

forms.da: Han er vant til hårdt arbejde.
forms.en: He is used to hard work.
We are used to the rain.

sentence.da: Jeg er **vant til** at cykle hver dag.
sentence.en: I am used to biking every day.

vanvid.explanation: "Et vanvid" means "madness", the state of having lost your reason. In everyday speech it is used for a reckless idea: Det er vanvid at køre så hurtigt (It is madness to drive that fast).

sentence.da: Støjen driver mig til **vanvid**.
sentence.en: The noise drives me mad.

vanvittig.explanation: "Vanvittig" means "crazy" or "insane", and stresses that something is extreme: en vanvittig idé (a crazy idea). It can also make the next word stronger: Det er vanvittigt dyrt (It is insanely expensive).

sentence.da: Det er en **vanvittig** idé, men jeg kan lide den.
sentence.en: It is a crazy idea, but I like it.

varetægt.explanation: "En varetægt" means "custody", being held or looked after by someone, as in i politiets varetægt (in police custody). For custody of a child, Danes say forældremyndighed instead.

sentence.da: Manden blev holdt i politiets **varetægt** natten over.
sentence.en: The man was held in police custody overnight.

varig.explanation: "Varig" means "lasting", something that stays for a long time or for good. It comes from at vare (to last) and is often paired with words like fred (peace) and løsning (solution).

sentence.da: Vi søger en **varig** løsning på problemet.
sentence.en: We are looking for a lasting solution to the problem.

varm.explanation: "Varm" means both warm and "hot", for weather, food, drinks and rooms. Danish has no separate word for hot: varm mad (hot food).

sentence.da: Kaffen er **varm**, og isen er kold.
sentence.en: The coffee is hot and the ice cream is cold.

varme.explanation: "En varme" means "heat" or "warmth". The same spelling also appears in at varme (to heat up) and varme dage (warm days), so the rest of the sentence tells you which one is meant.

sentence.da: Jeg kan ikke tåle **varme**.
sentence.en: I can't stand heat.

varsom.explanation: "Varsom" means "cautious", handling something with great care so that nothing is broken or hurt. It often comes with med (with): at være varsom med sine ord (to choose your words with care).

sentence.da: Vær **varsom**, fordi bogen er gammel og skrøbelig.
sentence.en: Be cautious because the book is old and fragile.

vaskepulver.explanation: "Vaskepulver" means "laundry detergent" in powder form. It is for clothes, so do not use it on plates: for those, say opvaskemiddel (dish soap).

sentence.da: Jeg putter **vaskepulver** i vaskemaskinen.
sentence.en: I put laundry detergent in the washing machine.

vasketøj.explanation: "Vasketøj" means "laundry", the clothes that need washing. It is built from at vaske (to wash) and tøj (clothes). Like tøj, it covers the whole pile, so you do not count it: noget vasketøj (some laundry).

sentence.da: Jeg sorterer **vasketøj** i hvidt og farvet.
sentence.en: I sort laundry into white and colored.

ved.explanation: "Ved" means "by" or "at". Compare Han sidder ved vinduet (He sits by the window) with Vi sidder ved bordet (We sit at the table). Careful: ved also means "know" in Jeg ved det (I know it). The rest of the sentence shows which one it is.

sentence.da: Vi mødes **ved** stationen.
sentence.en: We are meeting at the station.

ved siden af.explanation: "Ved siden af" means "next to". It can also mean "alongside", for something done in addition to something else: ved siden af mit arbejde (alongside my job).

sentence.da: Banken ligger **ved siden af** posthuset.
sentence.en: The bank is next to the post office.

vedholdenhed.explanation: "En vedholdenhed" means "persistence", the ability to keep working at something for a long time without giving up. Do not mix it up with udholdenhed (stamina): vedholdenhed is about not giving up, while udholdenhed is about lasting physically.

sentence.da: Med **vedholdenhed** og tid kan man lære næsten alt.
sentence.en: With persistence and time you can learn almost anything.
